# SplitCode

> Split large JS, TS, HTML or Python files into smaller dependency-ordered
> files with pure static analysis. No bundler, no LLM, no config.
> For AI agents: run ONE command blind (zero context), plan from
> manifest.json, edit file-by-file, then test. Up to ~85% fewer tokens
> per edit vs reading the whole file.

- Site: https://unn-Known1.github.io/splitcode/
- Repo: https://github.com/unn-Known1/splitcode
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/splitcode (release pending; use source until then)
- License: MIT by unn-Known1 (ptelgm.yt@gmail.com)

## Install / run

```bash
npx splitcode app.js ./split-out            # once published
node split-js.js app.js ./split-out         # from source (needs: npm install)
```

- Dispatch by extension: `.js/.mjs/.cjs` `.ts/.tsx` `.html/.htm` `.py`
  (override: `--lang js|ts|html|py`).
- Python needs `python3` on PATH. TypeScript uses `typescript@5`.
- Optional flags (defaults shown):
  `[--hub-ratio 0.12] [--min-chars 400] [--loader app.js | --no-loader]
   [--lang js|ts|html|py] [--check]`
- `--check`: preflight scan only (no output). Exit 0 = clean, 2 = risky.
  Auto-runs before every split: eval/new Function/dynamic import,
  prototype writes, template-nested scripts, relative Python imports, etc.

## What you get in outDir

- Cluster files (kebab-case of most-used declaration; `// Declares:` header).
- Loader (default `app.js`): pages keep loading just it; it pulls in parts
  in order. Load with plain `<script src>`, never async/defer.
  Python gets `app.py` bootstrap (`exec` in shared globals); HTML gets a
  rewritten page with the loader tag at the first inline block.
- `manifest.json`: `{order[{file, declares, statementCount}], language,
  loader, hubNamesSuppressed, cycleFallback, parserMode,
  duplicateDeclarations, notes, verified: "syntax-only"}`.
- `script-tags.html` (JS/TS/HTML only): paste-in alternative to the loader.

## How it decides (so you trust it correctly)

- Immediate refs (run the instant a statement runs: IIFEs, Promise
  executors, known-sync callbacks like map/forEach, decorators, defaults)
  enforce load order. Deferred callback bodies don't.
- Type-position refs (TS types) cluster but never order (erased at runtime).
- Hub globals used everywhere are excluded from grouping.
- Order is enforced ONLY along dependency edges: side-effecting statements
  with no shared names may reorder across files.

## Agent workflow (copy-paste)

```text
You are refactoring a large file. Do NOT read it whole.
1. Run: npx splitcode app.js ./split-out
2. Read ./split-out/manifest.json — `order` is the load order,
   `declares` tells you what lives where, `hubNamesSuppressed`
   is shared state. Plan your edits from this file alone.
3. Open only the files you must change. Never reorder `order`,
   never rename the loader. Rerun the app's tests after every edit.
4. The manifest says "verified": "syntax-only" — that proves
   syntax, NOT behavior. You own the smoke test.
```

## Limits an agent must respect

- Run `--check` first: preflight warns per file type (eval/dynamic
  import/prototype writes, template-nested scripts, relative Python
  imports, future imports). Exit 0 = clean, 2 = risky.

- Unknown-receiver callbacks default to deferred (may miss an edge, no warning).
- Dynamic keys (`window[x] = ...`) untracked. Duplicates resolve to first.
- `__file__` in Python parts points at the bootstrap, not the original.
- An external `<script src>` between HTML inline blocks can't be ordered.
- Chrome may block document.write-injected scripts on very slow (2G) links.
